pages.label: MCP servers unauthenticate CVEs
pages.body:
# MCP servers had a rough 48 hours: 4 unauthenticated CVEs

## Thesis

多个 MCP 服务器把工具接口裸奔上网, 认证缺失是系统性问题

## Notes

- 4 个 MCP 服务器的 HTTP/SSE 工具接口没设认证, 谁都能连 (CVSS 9.8/10.0)
- GitLab Workhorse 那个最狠: 工具调用能把服务器环境变量读出来 -- 字符串越过信任边界
- LiteLLM: 有认证检查, 但任意 Bearer token 都被当成合法 (假锁), 已确认被利用, 进了 CISA KEV
- CVE = 漏洞身份证号; CVSS = 严重程度打分; KEV = 正在被利用名单
- 研究连接: 没认证 = 系统不知道用户是谁 = 同意(consent)无处可挂, 同意机制直接失效

pages.title: The German Facebook Case
pages.label: The German Facebook Case
pages.body:
# Antitrust Economics at a time of upheaval: Chp14 The German Facebook Case

## Thesis

Facebook's supra-competitive data collection = abuse of dominance, equivalent to excessive pricing in a zero-price market

## Notes

- EU vs US: lack of post-Chicago analysis in EU cases; in Europe competition law is lawyers' realm
- Dominance: attention market - companies compete for user attention; active users determine dominance; user becomes the product
- Abuse / as-if competition: would yield social networks not requiring WhatsApp+Instagram data linkage
- Facebook zero-cost; supra-competitive data collection and usage = excessive pricing, enforceable only via dominant position
- Benchmarks for excess: price difference? profit margins? FCO: abuse = not respecting rules protecting consumers in unbalanced bargaining position
- super-profiles = quality deterioration = price increase in zero-price market
- harm starts when one market side imposes rules on the other ('take-it-or-leave-it'); FCO: consumers empowered vs dominant firms is prerequisite for competitive process
- competitors at disadvantage if they respected GDPR
- FCO ruling: bundling social network + massive personalized data collection; Hayekian: markets are decentralized info systems, competition needs meaningful options; giant data reservoir = entry barrier; consumers pay via data exploitation harm
- pros for users: efficiency. cons: data leaking; data collection may make users change behavior to please others/public bodies

## Question
作为现代的个体，我们之间应该保持怎样的距离？多少距离？何种形式的距离？Web3会让 "economic intimacy" 增强吗？

## Why it matters
* Clarifying how technological protocols, encryption, and spatial arrangements mediate human connection, autonomy, and privacy in modern economic and social interactions.

## Notes
- Vitalik: "Why I support privacy"
	  - privacy = not having to weigh too much other's behaviors before making decisions
	  - private/public games
- 建筑空间 $\rightarrow$ 公寓（一墙之隔）
	- "trust assumption"
	- "we go back to primitive tribe in Samoa where you adapted your life to a transparent society"
- David Friedman:
	-  e.g. "the conflict b/w realspace transparency and cyberspace privacy goes in the ..."
	  - "... It does no good to use strong encryption for my email if a video mosquito is sitting on the wall watching me type. So strong privacy in a transparent society requires some way of guarding the interface bt my real space body and cyberspace." 
- Richard Taylor: "Freedom, Anarchy, and the Law"
	  - p.7 "... my subjugation to such a man would depend upon the accident of my encountering him. In a political society on the other hand, an individual need not ever encounter those to whom he is subject.... Subjugation to them depends on no fortuities but on rules and established institutions."
	  - The game in the digital world, albeit seems to prevail nowadays, still has to be played on the physical level. Ironically, you have to keep your private key in a cold wallet and protect it using your physical body. But that might not be an irony. That might just be the balance between intimacy and privacy, 
- "1984" telescreens
- Web3 / DeFi $\rightarrow$ resume "barter"
- Ant / Econ: "economic intimacy"
- McLuhan: media > content
- 隐私还是联系？
	  - 什么 game 和这个矛盾密切相关？
	  - 什么加密技术 (Protocol) 与此相关？
	  - 信息不对称 $\rightarrow$ Mechanism Design
	  - DAO 的隐私保护与效率
	  - Goffman 表演理论 $\begin{cases} \text{前台} \\ \text{后台} \end{cases}$
- Transparency or Privacy?
- Foucault: Theory of body or psychiatry
- bomb & crypto - hacking in Iran. (June 20, 2025)
- [p.45 (To be linked)] p.45: Is Privacy a Norm? (The Privacy Paradox)
- Informal Insurance in Africa
	  - livestock insurance
	  - the impact of mobile money
- The Privacy Paradox.
    - Altman (1975) treats privacy as a dynamic, dialectic regulation process
    - A Superendowment Effect (Winegar, 2019) valuations of data privacy is expressive.
    - Gertrude Stein: "There is no there there."
- [p.56 (To be continued)]

## Question
If binary thinking tends to oversimplify complex things (realities), are ternary, quaternary, or more nuanced logical systems fundamentally different or better? Can this be examined using formal frameworks such as statistics, logic, or other mathematical theories?

## Why it matters
* Exploring whether non-binary logical systems provide a functionally superior or fundamentally distinct methodology for modeling complex systems, human judgment, and social phenomena compared to classical binary constraints.

## Next
* Review foundational papers on Multi-valued logic (MVL) and fuzzy logic applications in consumer preference or game theory.

## Notes
- Multi-valued logic / Multi-class classification
- Binary hypothesis testing
- Entropy
- Bayesian

  - expert systems & knowledge mining
  - Fuzzy preference & Consumer Theory
  - The "weights" in game theory payoff sheet(?)

- Weird "Induction Principle" sitting in the Qn of "How many genders should we have"?
